To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dispersal range of beetles and bugs that depend on recently dead asphen wood is about 100 m, and that this distance is strongly dependent on the availability of suitable habitat in the surrounding area.

1) the spatial scale at which the species richness of beetles and flat bugs dependent on recently dead wood responded to habitat connectivity was 93 m, and 2) the exposure of log-pile to the sun and high levels of connectivity increased the species diversity of aspen specialists.

the spatial scale at which aspen-specialist insects responded to habitat connectivity varied from 0.5 to 1.4 km and that the most important habitat features for these insects were the amount of aspen trees and the exposure of logs to the sun.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the colonisation of ephemeral habitat patches in a fragmented forest landscape.
the dispersal of beetles and bugs dependent on recently dead wood in boreal forests.
the colonisation of recently dead aspen logs by specialised species of beetles and flat bugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of the species studied, the spatial scale at which habitat connectivity has the strongest influence on species richness is 93 m, but this scale may be different for other species.
the most appropriate conservation strategy for a particular species depends on its dispersal ability.
the spatial scale of the response of species to habitat is species-specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that the spatial scale of response of species richness of asphen-specialist beetles and bugs was 93 m, and that the exposure of logs to sunlight, and high levels and connectivity of habitat increased species richness.
dead wood piles can be used to attract beetles and bugs, but the effect is species-specific and habitat connectivity is an important factor to consider.
the colonisation of ephemeral habitats by specialised species depends on the amount and spatial distribution of suitable habitat, but that this relationship is highly species-specific
The main takeaway from our work is that
conservation efforts should concentrate on sites where colonization by target species is the most probable.
restoration of habitat is most effective if the habitat is located in an environment where there is already a suitable habitat patch.
the conservation of aspen wood specialists in boreal forests may require a more active approach than in the case of many other forest insects.
